summary: Radar for 2026-11-18, all within the GLP-1 focus. The biggest new lead is the Boston 25 story (18 Nov) about an unexpected pregnancy on a GLP-1. It points straight at a label fact with strong search demand: both tirzepatide labels say the drug can make birth-control pills work less well. The FDA, the MHRA and ABC have all covered it, but our audience has seen little of it lately, which makes it the best label-change long video and Short this week. The holiday-table Shorts are at their peak now (Forbes "avoid the ER this holiday", 18 Nov). The NAION eye warning is still peaking (UC Davis and Good Housekeeping, 17–18 Nov, after the FDA action on 9 Nov) and needs a label-first angle with the absolute risk. SURMOUNT-ADOLESCENTS (JAMA, 15 Nov: BMI −18.5% vs +0.5%, n=160, ages 12–17) is everywhere but falls outside our adult audience, so it becomes a caution angle for parents. ScienceAlert has picked up the psychosis/mania case reports after stopping, so they're rising. Use them only inside the broad Stopping or Serious Risks videos. The always-on search-demand formats stay ranked high: pen/travel per the Instructions for Use, the what-to-expect series, the tirzepatide vs semaglutide head-to-head, hair loss, nausea and injection sites. Rejected: retatrutide "supplier" press releases, compounded/peptide sourcing, Medicaid/cost/coverage, and the old "brain reshaping" story recycled from May.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide (Mounjaro/Zepbound) and birth control pills: what the label says about the pill working less well, refreshed by this week's 'GLP-1 led to unexpected pregnancy' story
candidates.angle: Long video: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) and Birth Control: What Changes?' Answer by 15 s from the US label: tirzepatide may lower how well the pill is absorbed, mostly in the 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase. That's why the label advises a non-oral method or adding a barrier method during those windows. Explain gastric emptying as the reason (ties to How It Works). Add the label's pregnancy section and say plainly: plan this with your prescriber. No dosing, no 'stop the drug' line. Shorts: 'On tirzepatide and the pill? One label line to know.'
candidates.why_now: Boston 25 News (18 Nov) ran a 'surprise of her life' unexpected-pregnancy story, and the GLP-1 'pregnancy around use' thread (Danish 750k-pregnancy study) is already in our snapshots. This is a label fact with constant search demand ('mounjaro birth control'), and the mainstream regulatory coverage (MHRA, ABC) was months ago, so there's a fresh hook and a thin field. It fits the label-change search-demand format.

evidence.signal: Mass. woman says GLP-1 led to unexpected pregnancy
The FDA label advises a non-oral or barrier method for 4 weeks after starting and after each dose increase. The MHRA (UK) issued a similar warning.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide and the FDA's NAION eye warning: what the new label says, the absolute risk, and the symptoms that need same-day care
candidates.angle: Label-change long video or chapter, label first: 'Tirzepatide (Mounjaro) Eye Warning: How Rare Is It?'
